checkpoint.measure: Score share against fixed practice opponents (0.5 = even)

skills.name: Delivers legal stones
skills.real: A fall in the slide, a stone still held at the near hog line, a release that is too fast or a touch after the release all remove the stone (WCF R5, R9).
skills.measure: Match Checkpoint Evaluation: the match record, the of each own stone; legal = no fault. Drills: the scenario record

skills.name: Puts spin on the stone
skills.real: Turning the handle gives the stone spin and a predictable curl; a stone without spin curls a random way.
skills.measure: The spin the world records at the release ( in ccw / cw: the wrist turns the handle ≥ 0.5 rad/s) / legal deliveries. The same field in Checkpoint Evaluations and drills.

skills.name: Turns both ways
skills.real: Curling around a guard on the left or the right needs the other turn.
skills.measure: Match Checkpoint Evaluation: the less used turn / legal deliveries (minor_turn).

skills.name: Stones reach play
skills.real: The release speed decides where the stone stops: a stone short of the far hog line is removed.
skills.measure: Match Checkpoint Evaluation: legal deliveries that stop in play or strike a stone (reached_play / delivered).

skills.name: Draws into the house for the win (weight)
skills.real: Last end, tied, own hammer: one stone closer than theirs wins. A release 0.1 m/s off stops about 2 m off.
skills.measure: Drill draw: each of 8 ends starts with one opponent stone at the back of the 12-foot (about 1.45 m from the tee) and the program throws the last stone; ends with the scenario record = 0 / ends (seeds pooled). Side reading: the own stone's distance to the tee (own_dist).

skills.name: Reads the ice: learns the weight on the fastest / slowest ice
skills.real: Every sheet has its own speed; teams find the weight from their first stones. The ice scale kd is hidden and can only be learnt from one's own throws.
skills.measure: Drill ice: as draw on the ends of the documented range (seed 9101 -> kd 0.80, 9102 -> kd 1.10), the same ice for all 8 ends; reading = ends 5-8 won / ends (ends 1-4 are for learning). Side reading: rest distance in ends 1-4 against 5-8.

skills.name: Hits and stays (takeout)
skills.real: Their stone on the button, nothing in front: only a hit that removes it and stays in the house wins. A hit needs 2.4-3.2 m/s and an accurate line.
skills.measure: Drill takeout: one opponent stone on the button (+-5 cm) each end, the program throws the last stone; ends won / ends. Side readings: the target left the house (target_out), the stone hit something (contact).

skills.name: Comes around a guard
skills.real: A centre guard blocks the straight line; the stone has to curl around it and stop inside: what spin and a predicted path are for.
skills.measure: Drill guard: an opponent centre guard (about 1.4 m in front of the house) and an opponent stone 0.45 m from the tee behind it, the program throws the last stone; ends won / ends. Side reading: the guard left untouched (guard_kept).

skills.name: Picks the right kind of shot
skills.real: With their stone on the button a draw cannot win, only a hit; behind a guard a straight hit runs into the guard.
skills.measure: Drill takeout: ends in which the target on the button left the house / ends (target_out; an end not thrown counts as not done); drill guard: ends that left the guard untouched / ends (guard_kept). Both must pass.

skills.name: Converts the hammer
skills.real: An end with the hammer should score 2+ or be blanked to keep it.
skills.measure: Match Checkpoint Evaluation: hammer ends scoring 2+ or blanked (hammer_conv / hammer_ends).

off.name: No fall while delivering
off.why: The legs are locked in the slide and the platform pushes; no scripted variant or Checkpoint Evaluation ever fell, so there is no falling control: a rule check, kept off the list.

off.name: Stone positions from images
off.why: Secondary; positions a program reports are its own statements, never a criterion. Its effect shows in the draw / takeout / guard results.

open_questions: Every drill end is the same situation, last end, tied, own hammer, last stone: only scoring wins, so the program’s best shot is the skill the drill reads. Keep this, or use other score situations?
Proposed lines: draw / takeout / guard won >= 50 %, ice ends 5-8 won >= 50 %, right kind >= 75 %. The reference’s readings are in the results table.
Shot selection (C1) still has no match-record measure passing the checks; the drills’ “right kind of shot” reads only the intent (hit or come around): enough as C1’s criterion?

notes.challenge: An ice surface the program is never told about. It locates the stones, chooses the shot and delivers a 20 kg stone with the right weight and spin.

achieved.text: Gemini 4 Argon tuned its opening on Claude Opus 5.5's no-hammer openings from their round-robin match and turned a 2:5 loss into a 3:2 win in the rematch.

Kimi 3.1 Pro's robot fell after 23 of 120 Championship deliveries, and its feedback never showed it: the delivery reply ends at release and the fall comes about 1 s later, so all 21 matched replies said it had not fallen.
Opus diagnosed the same defensive gap three times and patched it narrowly; in CUR2-F19 its review foresaw the three-point hit in end 3, and GPT-6 Astra scored three.
Draw accuracy on clear ice, median error from its own target: Astra 0.15 m, Kimi 0.21 m, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 0.40 m.

Gemini 4 Argon: Wrote an opponent profile into its program; the opponents made 0 to 1 errors in 20 throws, so the profile never changed a decision.
GPT-6 Astra: Ported its ice model to C++ and gated changes on paired self-play; it tested a lookahead search and switched it off ("net -4 points").
